idiom_name: Enumerable#inject (alias reduce), block or symbol form
implementation_notes: Enumerable#inject is the fold and is available on every enumerable: inject(initial) { |memo, operand| ... } threads the block's return value (the docs are explicit that inject returns the memo, i.e. the last block result, not a mutated object), inject(:+) passes the operation as a symbol, and inject(initial, :+) adds an initial operand - reduce is documented as an alias. Two core methods cover the neighbouring cases without pretending to be folds: each_with_object(object) { |element, memo| ... } accumulates into a mutable object without reassigning the memo, and sum (Ruby 2.4+) plus min/max/count are the monoid specializations that pre-date a hand-written fold. Ruby has no right fold and no catamorphism for a recursive data type: a right-associative combine needs reverse_each/reverse or recursion, and a structural fold over nested hashes/arrays is a hand-written recursive method.
code_sketch:
total = orders.inject(0) { |sum, o| sum + o.amount }     # block form, explicit identity
nums  = [1, 2, 3, 4].inject(:+)                          # 10, symbol form
seed  = [1, 2, 3, 4].inject(10, :+)                      # 20 with the initial operand

by_city = orders.each_with_object(Hash.new(0)) { |o, h| h[o.city] += o.amount }
pitfalls: The block's last expression is the next memo: a block ending in puts, an append that returns the receiver, or a debug line collapses the fold into a wrong value, which is the main reason each_with_object is preferred for mutating accumulation.

The symbol form cannot take a block and the block form cannot take a symbol; inject(:+) on an empty array returns nil (there is no operand to seed from), so total-with-identity semantics need an explicit initial operand.

There is no right fold and no lazy fold: fold-right semantics require reverse_each or recursion, and each_with_object is not a fold because it never reassembles an accumulator, so code that substitutes it for inject gets the wrong shape.
